challenge.hint: "can't use" = {使|つか}えない. "Could you look at it?" (polite) = {見|み}ていただけますか.
challenge.model_answer: すみません、このカードが{使|つか}えないんですが、{見|み}ていただけますか。
challenge.prompt: Your card doesn't work at the ticket gate. Tell the station staff: "Excuse me, this card isn't working. Could you take a look?"

context: You've landed and need to reach your first volunteer host in the mountains. Today: topping up your IC card, finding the platform, and booking a seat at the ticket office.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, I'd like to go to Matsumoto.
dialogue.jp: すみません、{松本|まつもと}まで{行|い}きたいんですが。
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.jp: {特急|とっきゅう}ですか、{普通|ふつう}ですか。
dialogue.speaker: Staff

dialogue.en: Limited express, please. A reserved seat.
dialogue.jp: {特急|とっきゅう}でお{願|ねが}いします。{指定席|していせき}で。
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.en: There's the Azusa leaving at 10:00. Is a window seat all right?
dialogue.jp: 10{時|じ}{発|はつ}の「あずさ」がございます。{窓側|まどがわ}でよろしいですか。
dialogue.speaker: Staff

dialogue.jp: はい、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。{何番線|なんばんせん}ですか。
dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.jp: 9{番線|ばんせん}です。お{気|き}をつけて。
dialogue.speaker: Staff

dialogue_setting: At the ticket office ({みどりの窓口|みどりのまどぐち}) in Shinjuku.

kanji.related: Related: {出口|でぐち} exit, {乗換|のりかえ} transfer (often on orange signs).
kanji.where: On the overhead signs of every station. Follow it to get in or out. Big stations have several: {中央改札|ちゅうおうかいさつ} (central gates), {南改札|みなみかいさつ} (south gates).

phrases.en: I'd like to top up my IC card.
phrases.jp: ICカードにチャージしたいんですが。
phrases.note: ～たいんですが softens a request. Leave the sentence hanging and staff will help.

phrases.jp: {何番線|なんばんせん}ですか。
phrases.note: {番線|ばんせん} = platform number. You'll hear it in every announcement: 3{番線|ばんせん}に{電車|でんしゃ}が{参|まい}ります.

phrases.en: Does this train stop at Matsumoto?
phrases.jp: この{電車|でんしゃ}は{松本|まつもと}に{止|と}まりますか。
phrases.note: Ask this before boarding a rapid or express: they skip small stations.

phrases.jp: {乗|の}り{換|か}えはどこですか。

phrases.en: We're getting off at the next one.
phrases.note: With friends you drop the です/ます and add よ. {次|つぎ}の{駅|えき} shortens to just {次|つぎ}.

tip.body: In the countryside, many one-car trains and buses have no ticket gate. Board at the back, take a small numbered ticket ({整理券|せいりけん}) from the machine, then check the fare screen at the front for your number. Pay into the box by the driver when you get off. Most of them take IC cards now, but have coins ready just in case.
tip.title: Rural buses and trains: take a {整理券|せいりけん}

title_jp: {電車|でんしゃ}と{切符|きっぷ}

vocab.note: On station boards 普通 is the slowest train, stopping everywhere.
10時発 = leaving at 10:00. 東京発 = from Tokyo.
The aisle seat is {通路側|つうろがわ}.

vocab.en: there is (very polite あります)
